title: Participation Guarantee and Shortfall Charges under the Workplace Cafe Management Program
content:
Service models above the unsubsidised entry model of the Workplace Cafe Management Program are written against a participation guarantee: the share of the site's reported headcount the client undertakes will eat at the cafe.

**How participation is measured.** Participation is measured over the three complete billing periods before the one being invoiced, as the average number of distinct employees served per operating day against the reported headcount. A billing period in which service was suspended is left out of the average altogether.

**The shortfall charge.** Where measured participation falls below the guarantee printed against the service model, a shortfall charge is raised for each whole percentage point below it, at the rate printed against the same service model. Part points are not charged.

**When the shortfall charge is raised.** A shortfall charge is only raised while the contract stands active, suspended, or in transition out. It is never raised in the first three billing periods of a contract, because the measurement window is not yet complete. This is checked against the specific contract named in the request, using that contract's own status and its own service-commencement date on file, not a description the client gives of when service began.

**Where no guarantee applies.** Where the service model carries no participation guarantee, no shortfall charge is ever raised, however few employees eat at the cafe.

**Where the headcount report has changed.** Where the client's own headcount report has fallen since the contract was written, the guarantee is measured against the reported headcount in force on the invoice day rather than the headcount at signature.

**Parameters printed per service model.** Each of the six service models of the Workplace Cafe Management Program that carries a participation guarantee prints its own guarantee percentage of headcount, and its own shortfall rate charged per whole percentage point below the guarantee. No single figure is shared across all six service models for either.
